label: Text
name: The Sinic Classics Corpus
summary:
The Sinic Classics Corpus encompasses the foundational textual traditions of Chinese civilization, including the Confucian canon, the Daoist canon, and the Chinese historiographic tradition — collectively one of the richest and most continuous literary heritages in human history, spanning over 3,000 years. The Confucian Five Classics (Wujing) — the Classic of Changes (Yijing), Classic of Poetry (Shijing), Classic of History (Shujing), Classic of Rites (Liji), and Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) — formed the foundation of Chinese education and statecraft for over two millennia.

The Four Books (Sishu) — the Analects (Lunyu), Mencius (Mengzi), Great Learning (Daxue), and Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) — became the core of the Neo-Confucian curriculum and the basis of the imperial examination system (605–1905 CE) that selected Chinese government officials for 1,300 years. The Daoist canon (Daozang) — over 1,400 texts — preserves the mystical and naturalistic counter-tradition founded on the Dao De Jing and Zhuangzi.

The Twenty-Four Histories (Ershisi shi) represent the world's longest continuous state-sponsored historiographic tradition. Together, these texts shaped the civilization of 1.4+ billion Chinese and profoundly influenced Korea, Japan, Vietnam, and the broader East Asian world.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Sinic Classics Corpus has shaped Chinese civilization for over 3,000 years, influencing education, statecraft, and philosophy. Its Confucian canon and Neo-Confucian curriculum have had a profound impact on East Asian thought and culture.
